utah.temperature: Probabilities exceed 80% across most of the eastern CONUS, while odds drop further to the west due to troughing over the western CONUS, and near- to below-normal temperatures are most likely along the West Coast and western Great Basin.
utah.precipitation: Persistent troughing over the western CONUS results in a tilt towards above-normal precipitation across much of the Lower 48.

ne.temperature: Positive height anomalies over the North Pacific and eastern CONUS pair to keep cold Arctic air confined to higher latitudes and favor above-normal temperatures across most of the Lower 48.
ne.precipitation: -Canada border is likely to focus incoming moisture from the Pacific southward, resulting in near-normal precipitation favored over the Pacific Northwest, Northern Rockies, and Northern Plains, while increased moisture influx and low climatologies push odds of above-normal precipitation above 50% over portions of the Desert Southwest, as well as much of the central and eastern CONUS due to enhanced baroclinic instability and abundant Gulf moisture.

utah.temperature: As troughing moves further east into the West Coast, an increasing tilt towards below-normal temperatures is indicated for much of the West Coast and Great Basin, with chances exceeding 50% for portions of southern Nevada.
utah.precipitation: -Canada border keeps near-normal precipitation most likely for the Pacific Northwest, Northern Rockies, and Northern Plains.

ne.temperature: Otherwise, above-normal temperatures continue to be favored across the CONUS, with odds continuing to exceed 80% for portions of New England and at least above 50% for most areas east of the Rockies.
ne.precipitation: Above-normal precipitation remains most likely across much of the CONUS due to continued troughing over the West and weakening ridging over the East.

utah.temperature: Enhanced below-normal temperature probabilities are forecast over the Hawaiian Islands, and over parts of the southwestern CONUS, extending across Texas and southern Louisiana.

ne.temperature: The Temperature Outlook for weeks 3-4 indicates enhanced probabilities of warmer-than-normal temperatures along the West Coast of CONUS, and extending across the northern tier of CONUS, with maximum probabilities over New England.
